passages.title: A – FitPro Coach
passages.text: FitPro Coach creates a personal training plan for runners of every level and records your distance, speed and route on every run. You can join weekly challenges and compare your results with friends on the leaderboard. A one-week free trial is available, after which the app costs £4.99 a month.

passages.title: B – WildSpotter
passages.text: Take a photo of a flower, tree or bird and WildSpotter will tell you what it is in seconds. Before you set off, download the maps and wildlife guide for the area you're visiting, and the app will work perfectly even where there is no phone signal. You can also keep a diary of everything you've spotted.

passages.title: C – TalkTrip
passages.text: Learn the phrases you really need before your holiday with TalkTrip's ten-minute daily lessons in Japanese, Korean, Spanish and Italian. The app listens as you repeat each phrase out loud and tells you how to improve your pronunciation. By the end of the course, you'll be able to order food and ask for directions with confidence.

passages.title: D – BasketWise
passages.text: Before you go shopping, type in what you need and BasketWise will show you which local supermarket has the lowest prices for each item. It also tells you about special offers in shops near you. Your shopping list is saved on your phone, so you can tick things off as you go round the shop.

passages.title: E – FocusDesk
passages.text: Can't stop checking your phone while you study? FocusDesk blocks social media and games for as long as you choose. Tell it the dates of your exams and the subjects you're taking, and it will create a revision timetable for you, with short breaks built in. The basic version is free, with no adverts.

passages.title: F – LinguaBite
passages.text: LinguaBite offers five-minute lessons in over twenty languages, including Japanese and Arabic. Each lesson contains reading and writing exercises, and you can choose how many lessons a day you want to do. The app also builds a personal study plan for you and sends a reminder when it's time to practise.

passages.title: G – StrideTrack
passages.text: StrideTrack is completely free and records your distance, speed and route every time you go running, even with no phone signal. Invite your friends to join you, and the app will set fun challenges for your group each month – see who can run the furthest! You can also share photos of your runs.

passages.title: H – MealMap
passages.text: Choose your meals for the week from over 2,000 recipes, and MealMap will create a shopping list for you. To help you spend less, it suggests cheaper recipes and shows you how to use up leftovers. Everyone in the family can add items to the same list from their own phone, so nothing gets forgotten.

questions.question: Carlos is going to Japan next spring and wants to learn some useful Japanese first. He only has about ten minutes a day, and he is most worried about speaking.
questions.explanation: TalkTrip has 'ten-minute daily lessons in Japanese', and 'The app listens as you repeat each phrase out loud and tells you how to improve your pronunciation', which helps his speaking. LinguaBite also teaches Japanese in short lessons, but it only has 'reading and writing exercises'.

questions.question: Fiona wants to spend less on food for her family by planning the week's meals in advance. She'd like her husband and children to be able to add things to the shopping list too.
questions.explanation: With MealMap you 'Choose your meals for the week', it 'suggests cheaper recipes', and 'Everyone in the family can add items to the same list from their own phone'. BasketWise also helps you save money, but it does not plan meals and the list is only 'saved on your phone'.

questions.question: Jamal has just started running and wants an app that records his runs. He'd like to compete with his friends, but he doesn't want to pay anything.
questions.explanation: StrideTrack 'is completely free', 'records your distance, speed and route', and sets 'challenges for your group' so friends can 'see who can run the furthest'. FitPro Coach also records runs and lets you compare results with friends, but after the free trial it 'costs £4.99 a month'.

questions.question: Ellen goes walking in the hills every weekend and often sees plants and birds she doesn't know the names of. There's usually no mobile signal where she walks.
questions.explanation: WildSpotter tells you what 'a flower, tree or bird' is from a photo, and 'the app will work perfectly even where there is no phone signal'. StrideTrack also works 'with no phone signal', but it only records runs and cannot tell her the names of plants or birds.

questions.question: Kofi has important exams in June, but he keeps looking at social media instead of studying. He also needs help organising his revision so that he covers every subject.
questions.explanation: FocusDesk 'blocks social media and games' and, when you give it your exam dates and subjects, 'it will create a revision timetable for you'. LinguaBite also 'builds a personal study plan', but only for language lessons, and it does not stop him using social media.
